tools.name: chat
tools.description: Run a query through MarketIntell's brain (auto-routes to T1 fast agent or T2 CoT pipeline based on intent). Returns synthesized analysis with citations and trade setup when relevant.

tools.name: chat_deep
tools.description: Run a query through MarketIntell's T3 supervisor — parallel specialists across technical/derivatives/macro/social/onchain/etc. plus synthesis. Slower (~25-40s) and costlier than `chat`. Pro tier only.

tools.name: alpha_signals
tools.description: Fetch recent alpha signals — automated market intelligence. Crypto signals every ~10 min; equities (Beta) every ~30 min during US market hours. Filter by domain to narrow.

tools.name: signal_performance
tools.description: Realized signal accuracy — rolling 30-day win rate over CLOSED trade signals, where a win is a real take-profit / in-profit expiry (net positive after fees & leverage) and a loss is a real stop-loss / losing expiry. Win-rate is over resolved signals only; flat (break-even) and cancelled/no-fill/ambi

tools.name: screener
tools.description: Token screening — find trending tokens, top gainers, and top losers. Use this to discover what's moving in the market right now.

tools.name: portfolio_list
tools.description: List all portfolios owned by the authenticated key. Returns id, name, holdings, timestamps.

tools.name: portfolio_create
tools.description: Create a new portfolio for the authenticated key. Holdings are token symbol + amount (+ optional entry_price and notes).

tools.name: portfolio_analyze
tools.description: Compute PnL + risk assessment for a portfolio you own. Returns per-holding pnl, risk_assessment, and top_risks.

tools.name: sessions_list
tools.description: List the authenticated key's recent chat sessions. Useful to resume prior conversations.

tools.name: billing_status
tools.description: Return the authenticated key's plan, daily quota usage, monthly LLM-cost-cents, and cap. Mirrors GET /v1/billing/status.

tools.name: health
tools.description: MarketIntell system health — uptime, cache stats, memory, provider circuit-breaker states.

tools.name: register_challenge
tools.description: Step 1 of MCP self-signup. Returns a proof-of-work challenge. Solve locally (find a nonce whose sha256 has the required leading zero hex chars), then call `register` with { challenge_id, nonce, name }.

tools.name: register
tools.description: Step 2 of MCP self-signup. Submit the challenge id + solved nonce to provision a fresh Free-tier API key. The key is shown ONCE — store it. Pro upgrades go through Stripe checkout; this tool only issues Free keys.

tools.name: execute_propose_intent
tools.description: Propose a trade intent to the user's connected broker. Writes a pending row the user reviews + approves. Requires `trade` scope. Use this when an agent wants to act on a signal without placing the order itself.

tools.name: execute_approve_intent
tools.description: Approve a pending trade intent and place the order at the broker. Returns the executed_order audit row. Requires `trade` scope.

tools.name: execute_list_intents
tools.description: List the caller's recent trade intents (pending, executed, rejected). Requires `trade` scope.

tools.name: execute_read_portfolio
tools.description: Read the caller's connected broker account snapshot — equity, cash, buying power, open positions. Requires `trade` scope.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: sessions_list · Private data: screener, portfolio_create, register · Public sink: register · Destructive: chat, chat_deep, execute_propose_intent, execute_approve_intent, execute_list_intents, execute_read_portfolio.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: sessions_list · Private data: screener, portfolio_create, register · Public sink: register · Destructive: chat, chat_deep, execute_propose_intent, execute_approve_intent, execute_list_intents, execute_read_portfolio

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
